stemBlocks.value: Make a the subject of the formula v = u + at.
Think first: a is multiplied by t and the whole product is added to u, so undo the addition first.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p095-q07 from workbook page 95.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the new subject on the left.

strategyBlocks.value: Subtract u from both sides to isolate at, then divide by t.

whyThisWorks.value: Reversing a formula means undoing its operations in the opposite order to how they were applied: at was formed by multiplication and then added to u, so subtraction comes first and division second. Keeping v − u inside a bracket before dividing ensures the whole difference is divided by t, not just the v.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing a = v − u/t, so only u is divided by t.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing a = v − u/t, so only u is divided by t.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing by t before subtracting u.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing by t before subtracting u.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing a = (u − v)/t with the subtraction the wrong way round.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing a = (u − v)/t with the subtraction the wrong way round.

examTip.value: When a whole expression is divided, write it over a fraction bar or in brackets — a = (v − u)/t is safe, a = v − u/t is a different formula.
